title: Why Is China Proposing Reciprocal Nuclear Laboratory Visits?
author: Ying Zhang
text:
Crews at Los Alamos National Laboratory in New Mexico, the U.S., repackage waste to be shipped to the Waste Isolation Pilot Plant, Dec. 20, 2011.
Credit: U.S. Department of Energy
On October 6, CNN reported that the United States and China are engaged in informal, preliminary discussion on reciprocal visits to nuclear facilities. According to the report, the idea was first raised by the Chinese side in meetings with U.S. officials this year, during which the two sides discussed U.S. Department of Energy national laboratories and their Chinese counterparts. The same source also indicated that the U.S. side is willing to discuss visits to nuclear test sites. At the China-U.S. leaders’ summit held in September, the two sides agreed to build “a constructive relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness, and reciprocity.” According to CNN, however, they didn’t discuss reciprocal nuclear facility visits at the summit.[...]
